name: Online Booking & Appointment Scheduling – Vigore
author: devvigore

sections.description:
Vigore adds online booking and appointment scheduling to your WordPress site. The plugin connects your site to your free Vigore account and embeds your booking flow as a widget, so your customers can book any timeslot based service directly from your pages. It is fully responsive and works on every device.

Unlike a calendar bolted into wp-admin, Vigore is a complete booking system: appointments, online payments, automated reminders, calendar sync and a client portal, all managed from one place. And because your booking flow is a widget, you can embed the same experience on any site, not just WordPress.

After you install and activate the plugin, an onboarding starts automatically and guides you through the entire setup, so your booking widget is live in minutes.

Vigore Widget works together with the Vigore booking platform at vigore.app. See the Vigore Terms of Use and Privacy Policy.

What you can do

  • Take online bookings for appointments and timeslot based services
  • Accept payments through Stripe and PayPal (Stripe also covers iDEAL, cards, Apple Pay and Google Pay)
  • Send automated booking reminders to reduce no shows
  • Sync bookings with Google Calendar and Outlook / Microsoft 365
  • Manage clients and appointments from your Vigore dashboard (CRM and client portal)
  • Show multiple professionals or team members and let customers pick
  • Available in Dutch and English, with pricing in euro, US dollar or British pound
  • Add the booking widget to your site without any coding

Who it is for

Vigore works for any service business that books time, whether you take appointments or hourly reservations:

  • Personal trainers taking session and package bookings
  • Coaches running 1 on 1 and program based work
  • Nutritionists and lifestyle coaches scheduling consultations
  • Salons and barbershops booking appointments across a team
  • Driving schools filling lesson slots
  • Rental businesses renting equipment or gear by the hour
  • Venues and meeting rooms booked by the hour or slot
  • Consultants and advisors offering paid intro and follow up calls
  • Therapists and wellness practitioners managing a calendar of clients
  • Studios and multi person teams coordinating several professionals

Not your typical WordPress booking plugin

Most booking plugins store everything inside your WordPress site, and you manage it all from wp-admin. Vigore works differently: the plugin connects your site to your free Vigore account and embeds your booking flow as a widget. Your bookings, clients, payments and settings live in Vigore, a complete booking platform, managed from one dashboard.

Why that helps you:

  • Embed anywhere. The same booking experience on WordPress, Squarespace, Shopify and more, not locked to one site.
  • Nothing to maintain. No heavy plugin or database to manage, and your booking system is always up to date.
  • More than a calendar. Booking, CRM, payments, reminders and a client portal in one place.
  • Free to get started. Works with a free Vigore account.

How it works

  1. Install and activate the plugin.
  2. Connect your free Vigore account. An onboarding guides you through the entire setup.
  3. Your booking widget goes live on your site.

Useful links

  • Vigore website
  • Pricing (free to get started)
  • Frequently asked questions
  • Terms of Use
  • Privacy Policy
  • Support

External services

This plugin connects your site to the Vigore booking platform at vigore.app to provide online booking. To do this it communicates with the Vigore API at https://api.vigore.app and displays the booking widget served from https://widget.vigore.app.

The plugin sends requests to https://api.vigore.app in these cases:

  • When you connect your site, to set up and verify the connection to your Vigore account.
  • Periodically (about once a day) while connected, a status “heartbeat” that sends your site URL, your connection identifier, the plugin version and your WordPress version so the connection stays active.
  • To check whether the connection is still active, and to disconnect the site when you remove it.
  • Once, when the plugin is activated on a site that is not yet connected, an “install ping” that sends your site URL, the plugin version and your WordPress version so we can recognise the installation. No email address or personal account data is sent by this request.

To display the booking widget on your site, your public pages load it as an iframe from https://widget.vigore.app. The widget URL includes your Vigore organization identifier (and professional identifier, if set) so the correct booking calendar is shown to your visitors.

Data you submit to the Vigore platform is governed by the Vigore Terms of Use (https://vigore.app/terms) and Privacy Policy (https://vigore.app/privacy-policy).
sections.installation:
1. In your WordPress admin, go to Plugins > Add New and search for “Vigore”.
  2. Click Install Now, then Activate.
  3. Open Vigore Widget in the admin menu (it appears in the left-hand menu).
  4. Connect your free Vigore account.
  5. Finish the onboarding (about 5 minutes), which guides you through the full setup.
  6. The booking widget appears on your site.
sections.faq:
Is the Vigore Widget free?

Yes. The plugin is free and works with a free Vigore account.

Do I need a Vigore account?

Yes. The widget works with your free Vigore account, where your bookings and settings live. The onboarding helps you create one, including with Google login.

Can I take payments through the booking widget?

Yes. Vigore supports payments through Stripe and PayPal. Stripe also covers iDEAL, debit and credit cards, Apple Pay and Google Pay.

Where does the booking widget appear on my site?

After you connect your account and finish the onboarding, the booking widget appears on your site.

Can I choose which professionals are shown?

Yes. You select the professionals to display during onboarding and in the plugin settings.

Does it sync with Google Calendar or Outlook?

Yes. Vigore syncs with Google Calendar and Outlook / Microsoft 365.

Is the booking widget mobile friendly?

Yes. The widget is fully responsive and works across phones, tablets and desktops.

Can I use Vigore on a website that is not WordPress?

Yes. Because the booking flow is a widget, you can embed the same experience on other sites too, such as Squarespace or Shopify.

How is this different from a normal WordPress booking plugin?

A typical booking plugin stores everything inside WordPress and you manage it from wp-admin. Vigore is a booking platform: your site connects to your Vigore account, the booking flow appears as a widget, and you manage bookings, clients and payments from your Vigore dashboard.

Where is my booking data stored?

Your bookings, clients and settings are stored in your Vigore account on the Vigore platform. See the Vigore Terms of Use and Privacy Policy linked in the description.
sections.changelog:
2.3.6

  • Fix: the booking button no longer disappears when an accessibility plugin (e.g. Elementor “Web Accessibility / Ally”) applies a colour filter such as Grayscale or Contrast to the page. The button now stays pinned to the corner regardless of such filters.
  • Improve: when another floating control shares the same screen corner (an accessibility button, chat widget or cookie bar), the booking button steps aside automatically — it moves up so it sits above the other button (both stay visible), and hides itself while an accessibility panel is open, then returns when the panel is closed.

2.3.5

  • Fix: the booking launcher could be hidden behind other site elements (cookie bars, chat widgets, overlays); it now sits above them.

2.3.4

  • Fix: the collapsed booking button now fits the English label (“Make an appointment”) when the widget language is set to English.

2.3.3

  • Recognise new installations so we can support you even before you finish connecting your site.
  • Documented the external Vigore services the plugin communicates with.

2.3.2

  • Fix: the booking widget now appears for logged-out visitors on sites with full-page caching (FlyingPress, WP Rocket, LiteSpeed, WP Super Cache, etc.). The widget is loaded on the client from a non-cached status endpoint, so connecting, disconnecting or changing its settings no longer requires clearing the page cache.
  • The cache is refreshed automatically once after this update, so an already-connected site starts showing the widget without any manual action.
  • Align the reported plugin version across the heartbeat and status endpoints.

2.3.1

  • Refreshed the plugin listing and onboarding copy.
  • Tested up to WordPress 7.0.

2.3.0

  • Enable WordPress dashboard connect flow: connect your site directly from the Vigore dashboard
  • Add rate limiting for pending connection polling (once per minute)
  • Add remote disconnect detection: the widget deactivates when disconnected from the dashboard
  • Improve login error handling for unverified or unfinished accounts
  • Bump plugin version to 2.3.0

2.2.0

  • Added automatic site connection from the Vigore dashboard
  • Added daily heartbeat to track plugin status
  • Added widget active/inactive toggle via dashboard disconnect
  • Minor improvements and stability fixes

2.1.0

  • Update to new Vigore APIs

2.0.1

  • Fixed API endpoint URL for instructor fetching
  • Improved widget state management and sizing
  • Fixed asset loading hook for better compatibility
  • Enhanced widget responsiveness

2.0

  • Major update: per user Vigore authentication and UI/UX enhancements

1.0

  • Initial release of Vigore Widget
